title: Tinn articulated demonstrator
status: Source-led educational mechanical completion, not a recovered design or a flightworthy aircraft.

source_reading.readable: Mute swan planform: broad arm wing, rounded tapered hand wing. Rounded Say span 7.4 ft, wrist span 3.7 ft = 50% b. Original wing-area paragraph gives 6.61 square feet and AR about 8.29.
source_reading.used: aspect_ratio = 7.4 squared / 6.61 = 8.284417549167928; wrist_span_fraction = 3.7 / 7.4 = 0.5. Full-size area is 14 squared / aspect_ratio, approximately 23.658 square metres. Broad inner chord and rounded outer ellipse retained by the supplied four-segment planform helper.
source_reading.uncertain: Exclude the inconsistent 3.135 ft wing-length conversion. Handwritten alterations around the area paragraph and its specimen comparison do not establish a replacement measurement.
source_reading.completion: 14 m span, central hinge gap, taper ratio and curved material-coordinate geometry are supplied engineering assumptions.

source_reading.readable: Göttingen 417a curved plate chart, with lift, drag and moment axes and low Reynolds-number annotations including roughly 168000 and 42000.
source_reading.used: Separate inner and outer section descriptions; no numerical full-scale chart digitisation claimed.
source_reading.uncertain: Multi-axis scales, curve associations and pencilled readings are ambiguous; exact coefficients are not recovered.
source_reading.completion: All section arrays, endpoint clamping, camber lift increments and finite-span induced drag are the supplied illustrative full-scale model.

source_reading.readable: Bird flight as a guide to ornithopter design, Stanley J. O. Tinn, 2007. Define an ideal sine trajectory; cruising speed and flapping frequency determine the required range of vertical forces. Evaluate candidate wing actions using steady-state aerodynamics. Manned mechanical flight is the stated objective.
source_reading.used: The existing force-comparison panel compares candidate forces with the required trajectory; free flight integrates actual forces, never a prescribed path. A visible seated adult operates the aircraft.
source_reading.uncertain: Some handwritten historical revisions cannot be read confidently and are not used as engineering data.
source_reading.completion: Pilot 55 kg, clothing, helmet, seating, engine power and cockpit controls are modern supplied/design additions.

source_reading.readable: Straight and level flapping flight cannot be exactly steady: cyclic lift and thrust produce an undulating path and unsteady airspeed. Bounding and ring-gait flight are discussed. The opening refers explicitly to a powered man-carrying ornithopter.
source_reading.used: Cyclic strip forces and real wing/body motion remain visible; no smoothing of the physics or direct thrust is added.
source_reading.uncertain: The marginal handwritten sentence is not used quantitatively; missing appendices remain missing.
source_reading.completion: A finite-torque petrol engine drives the mechanism rather than biological muscle or pilot pedalling.

source_reading.readable: At low speed flap down lasts longer than recovery; periods become equal as speed increases. Wing-wishbone-body assembly can be resonant. Compare lift and drag of candidate actions against the desired force variation. Fore/aft CG oscillation accompanies cyclic thrust.
source_reading.used: Fixed timing-bias linkage settings 0.3 and 0; a coupled spring/inertia model; honest required-versus-candidate force comparison.
source_reading.uncertain: Crossed-out double-parabola passage and extensive marginal revisions do not define unambiguous revised numerical equations.
source_reading.completion: theta = phi - b sin(phi), spring stiffness, inertia and all numerical phase curves are supplied mechanical completions, not notebook samples. No in-flight automatic timing change.

source_reading.readable: Wing and body inertia plus wishbone springiness exchange energy. Fore/aft wing motion changes CG/centre-of-lift separation and pitches the body. Wing action uses arm and hand portions: forward recovery, opening and pulling down/back; closing during recovery.
source_reading.used: Actual distributed wing masses, CG reaction, coupled phase and pitch coordinates, sweep linkage and two overlapping sliding outer leaves. Lift/drag directions use actual local motion.
source_reading.uncertain: No complete mechanical linkage dimensions or validated full-scale spring curve are given.
source_reading.completion: The supplied helper constructs mass geometry and derivatives from our wingPose. Half-length rigid sliding leaves implement closing without deleting hidden mass; tail and passive pitch damping are engineering additions.

source_reading.readable: Opening continuation: reduced area and span on recovery, repetition of cycle, local incidences optimise thrust and drag; pencilled addition mentions camber. Later goshawk example has different proportions and lists 13%, 10%, 9%, 6% camber.
source_reading.used: Recovery overlap changes exposed span; incidence and changing camber remain independent geometric and aerodynamic quantities.
source_reading.uncertain: The goshawk percentages and figure dimensions are not swan specifications and are not copied.
source_reading.completion: Supplied small inner and outer camber curves produce curved geometry and section-coefficient changes independently of twist. Exposure and camber laws are explicit assumptions.

source_reading.readable: Arm section 5 to 6 percent thick, outer hand wing a thin slotted curved plate. Local trajectory tilts lift and drag into thrust/vertical directions; closing reduces recovery drag. Conventional tail/weight shift and a longer-arm fin/rudder suit an ornithopter. Swan takeoff discussion includes arm -15 to +45 degrees and hand +/-45 degrees.
source_reading.used: 5.5% inner thickness metadata, thin curved outer fabric, visible articulation, conventional tail/elevator and rudder, three-wheel rolling takeoff.
source_reading.uncertain: Biological takeoff angles are context, not full-scale aircraft linkage limits; no aircraft performance guarantee is inferred.
source_reading.completion: Supplied stroke amplitudes, 0.8% outer structural thickness, local strip aerodynamics, controls and landing-gear contact model replace unspecified mechanical details. Decorative ribs and spars do not add unbudgeted simulated mass.

source_reading.readable: Baseline glide drag Dg = W divided by L/D; glide power Dg V / 550 in horsepower. Extra powered-flight costs include induced drag, horizontal acceleration, vertical trajectory and wing inertia. Inertial power is zero without damping in the ideal model. Design algorithm refers to Appendix 12.
source_reading.used: Aerodynamic drag work, translation, coupled rotational kinetic energy and hinge spring energy are accounted for. Spring energy is storage, never a net source. Motor-off motion coasts under the same equations.
source_reading.uncertain: Missing appendices, bracketed references and pencilled scaling notes do not supply a complete power model.
source_reading.completion: 16 kW shaft limit, 85% transmission, finite starting torque, 300 kg m2 reflected inertia, fuel BSFC, damping coefficients and RK2 integration are supplied engineering assumptions, not Stanley's numbers.

engineering.mass_allocations: Supplied revised engineering mass_budget, including all 30 kg of wings during overlap.
engineering.neutral_stability: Passive pitch damping 1000 N m s/rad, dissipating coefficient times pitch_rate squared; no trim autopilot or altitude hold.
engineering.ground_model: Three-wheel pitch-zero constrained reduction, Ag and Agp include vertical whole-CG reaction. Constraint releases only when normal load would be negative. Actual terrain and rotated CG correction determine tyre contact.
engineering.integration: Midpoint RK2 with substeps no larger than 1/240 second. Airborne two-coordinate Lagrange solve. No arbitrary phase stopping on throttle removal.
engineering.glide: Explicit frozen extended configuration only when state.gliding is true; neutral unpowered glide uses engineering.glide. Approach is already-powered flight at the supplied 16 m/s, pitch 0.1, omega 6 and 90% throttle; initial kinetic energy belongs to its initial condition.
engineering.visual_language: Ivory translucent sailcloth, graphite-green tubular truss, bronze hinge springs, exposed finned engine and belt reduction, sliding leaf spars, long conventional tail, teal open cockpit and helmeted seated pilot. Tyres rotate about lateral z axles.
engineering.causal_interventions: motor_enabled, gravity, rho, pitch_locked, damping_scale, pose override and sweep_scale all act on the same production model.

limitations: Illustrative favourable lightweight mass budget, not structurally validated or experimentally flight-validated.
Quasi-steady low-strip-count model omits wake history, unsteady stall, section pitching moments, flexible wing motion and flow interaction between overlapping leaves.
Roll/yaw inertial coupling is omitted; horizontal rudder force and finite roll controls are reduced controls.
Three-wheel rigid contact is not a suspension model. Touchdown projection dissipates energy; it is not a source of flight energy.
Visual fittings represent the allocated components, not additional independently simulated masses.
No tests, code execution, builds or visual previews were performed under the file-only protocol.
Historical source references and handwritten marginal revisions are incomplete; no invented recovered data or missing appendices are claimed.
